key_insight: Instead of allocating a distinct expert set to each transformer layer, a single globally shared expert pool (UniPool) can serve all layers—maintaining accuracy while breaking the linear growth of expert parameters with depth.
problem_solved: Fixes the rigid per-layer expert allocation in MoE models that couples depth scaling to linear expert-parameter growth and assumes each layer needs isolated expert capacity, leading to inefficient parameter use.
method: Introduce UniPool: one globally shared set of experts that all transformer layers can route to, replacing per-layer expert partitions.
Use a layer-agnostic routing/gating scheme (top-k selection from the global pool) with load-balancing and capacity management to avoid hotspots.
Empirically validate via routing probes and downstream evaluations showing negligible accuracy loss with far fewer expert parameters.
impact: Enables more parameter-efficient MoE scaling (deeper models without proportional expert-parameter growth), simplifies MoE design choices, and reduces training/inference cost for practitioners.
visual_elements: Schematic comparison: traditional per-layer experts vs. UniPool (shared pool) with arrows showing routing paths.
Bar chart: expert-parameter count vs. downstream accuracy for per-layer MoE and UniPool.
Heatmap of routing assignments: layer-to-expert usage illustrating cross-layer sharing in UniPool.
Icon set: expert pool (pool icon), gating mechanism (switch/gauge), and efficiency (downward cost arrow)
paper_title: UniPool: A Globally Shared Expert Pool for Mixture-of-Experts
paper_authors: Minbin Huang, Han Shi, Chuanyang Zheng, Yimeng Wu, Guoxuan Chen
